paragraphs: R' Yissa Kotzarya, son-in-law of R' Yosi.
Mentioned in Bava Batra, chapter 10, halakhah 1, reporting in the name of his father-in-law.[^1][^2]

notes.text: Kotzarya transliterates קוצריא without deciding its meaning. חתניה gives son-in-law, and the body has him reporting his father-in-law. Earlier machine קצירא חנניה differs from supplied קוצריא חתניה; provisional heading status is not newly adjudicated.
ב״ב פ״י ה״א gives Bava Batra chapter 10 halakhah 1. The format suggests the Jerusalem Talmud, but no corpus is stated or independently checked. Both personal title abbreviations remain R'.
